key_insight: The paper shows that fault-tolerant quantum computers could simulate atomic nuclei using nuclear Hamiltonians, with resource costs that are promising for some shell-model cases but much higher for light-nucleus no-core calculations.
engineering_relevance: This extends quantum simulation beyond chemistry and suggests where near-term fault-tolerant architectures may need optimization to make nuclear-structure applications practical.
method: Constructed quantum algorithms for effective shell-model Hamiltonians.
Extended the approach to no-core-shell-model Hamiltonians with chiral EFT three-body interactions.
Compiled fault-tolerant resource estimates in Toffoli gates and qubits.
evidence_signal: The authors report the first resource estimates for fault-tolerant quantum simulation of atomic nuclei and compare shell-model cases such as 32Mg and 219At to recent Femoco chemistry benchmarks.
watch_item: No-core-shell-model simulations for light nuclei remain far more resource-intensive, so practical use will likely require more specialized algorithms or hardware-aware optimizations.
paper_title: Fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for simulating atomic nuclei
